subject: FinTrust — proof of export, auth, and on-prem proxy requirements
messages:
From: Simon Leary <simon.leary@fintrust.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.ai>
Cc: security@fintrust.com
Date: Mon, 19 Mar 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Observability export proof / auth model questions

Priya,

Thanks for taking this on. Our security team needs concrete answers before we greenlight the private deploy: a short checklist would help. Specifically we need:

- Preferred export modes: push to FinTrust SIEM (Splunk/HEC) vs pull from our side, or using Redwood-hosted forwarder in our VPC.
- Auth: mutual-TLS + client certs, HEC token only, or IP allowlist? Which do you support and which do you recommend for on-prem?
- Evidence: sample logs (anonymized) and proof that exports do not leak customer PII (scrubbing/redaction options).
- Network: outbound port + IP ranges to open, and whether a bastion/proxy is required for air-gapped segments.
- Audit: retention of delivery/audit events (who pulled/pushed, timestamps) and rotation policy for long-lived tokens.

Attached is our standard evidence request (fintrust-evidence-request-v2.pdf) — if you can fill the key fields and return sample logs that'd be great. Also: can Redwood provide a short runbook for the forwarder lifecycle (install, rotate creds, revoke, troubleshooting)?

Simon
Security Architect
FinTrust Bank

--
[Attachment: fintrust-evidence-request-v2.pdf (application/pdf)]

From: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.ai>
To: Simon Leary <simon.leary@fintrust.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 20 Mar 2028 11:07:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Observability export proof / auth model questions

Hi Simon — thanks for the detailed checklist and the PDF. Quick summary up front: we can support both directions (push and pull) but for FinTrust's requirements we recommend deploying a Redwood-managed forwarder inside your VPC (option A) with mTLS to Redwood's ingress, or configuring export directly to your Splunk HEC endpoint (option B) with HEC token + client certs. Below are the details and attachments.

Option A — Redwood forwarder in customer VPC (recommended for regulated on-prem):
- Deploy a lightweight container (Linux) in the FinTrust app subnets. Runs the Redwood forwarder (systemd/container).
- Authentication: mutual TLS using customer-generated client certs; Redwood verifies cert CN against the registered host. We additionally implement short-lived session tokens for connection-level audit.
- Network: outbound 443 to these egress endpoints: 34.212.8.123, 34.212.8.124 (Redwood ingress cluster). If you prefer a FQDN we can provide wildcard certs.
- Scrubbing: built-in pipeline supports field-level redaction (PII regexes) and hash-replacement. We attach a sample redaction profile.
- Audit: forwarder emits delivery events to a local audit file and also to a separate audit topic retained for 90 days by default (configurable).
- Rotation: cert rotation handled by your Ops; we recommend rotating client certs every 90 days; session tokens rotate hourly.
- Attachments: redwood-sample-forwarder-logs.jsonl (anonymized), network-egress-diagram.png

Option B — Direct to customer Splunk HEC (fastest to stand up):
- HEC TLS endpoint on FinTrust side. Redwood will push to it over TLS with HEC token + optional client cert.
- We recommend mTLS + HEC token for defense-in-depth.
- Firewall: FinTrust to allow Redwood egress IPs (above) or allow FQDN and validate certs.

Notes on air-gapped / bastion scenarios:
- For segments without direct egress, we support a bastion transfer pattern: forwarder -> local staging gateway -> scheduled pull by an ops-side bundle transfer. This induces >30s latency for delivery but preserves custody chain.

Runbook + evidence: attached a single-file runbook (redwood-onprem-runbook-v1.4.md) and a set of sample anonymized logs. I filled the fields in your PDF where possible and returned it in the Drive link below.

Next steps: if this looks good I suggest a 45‑minute architecture review with your security and network teams. Kimberly (cc'd) and I will join.

Priya Natarajan
Product Security & Integrations
Redwood Inference

Attachments referenced: redwood-sample-forwarder-logs.jsonl, network-egress-diagram.png, redwood-onprem-runbook-v1.4.md

[Drive link: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3cFinTrust-ObsvAssets]

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: Simon Leary <simon.leary@fintrust.com>, Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 21 Mar 2028 08:34:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Observability export proof / auth model questions

Simon — quick security addendum from the compliance team. Two points we need to confirm for FinTrust acceptance:

1) Proof of delivery / non-repudiation: can Redwood provide signed delivery receipts for each batch (signature + timestamp) and a searchable audit log export for those receipts? We typically deliver receipts as a small JSON envelope signed by Redwood KMS.

2) Redaction guarantees: please confirm exact fields you want scrubbed; we will implement a test pipeline. Also need to confirm if truncated hashing (one-way) is acceptable or if you require tokenization with key-handling on your side.

We'll prepare a short evidence bundle (SOC2 + packaged audit receipts) prior to the architecture review. Priya — can you add token rotation cadence and where the receipts land in the runbook?

Kimberly Park
Head of Compliance Integrations
Redwood Inference

[Attachment: none in this message]

From: Simon Leary <simon.leary@fintrust.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 22 Mar 2028 10:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Observability export proof / auth model questions

Thanks Kimberly — hashed + truncated IDs are acceptable for most of our telemetry, but we will ask the data governance team for a short list of fields that must be redacted vs hashed. We also want the signed receipts and a way to pull a bundle of receipts for a given date range (api or s3 export).

A couple of follow-ups:
- Can the runbook include an emergency revoke flow (e.g., compromise of client certs) with step-by-step commands?
- For the bastion/pull option, what is the expected operational window for evidence pickup? (we have batch windows at 01:00 and 13:00 local)

I'll assemble the redaction list and loop in our network engineer for the ports.

Simon

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Simon Leary <simon.leary@fintrust.com>, Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 23 Mar 2028 16:48:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Observability export proof / auth model questions

Simon — looping in ops/solutions. I've created a short implementation plan in JIRA (JIRA-OBSV-4217) and a shared architecture review invite for next week. A couple practical items from the runbook we've attached:

- Emergency revoke: run 'redwood-forwarder revoke-client --cert <CN>' on the control plane, rotate the gateway session token, and confirm on both sides. We also publish a revocation event to the customer's audit topic — runbook section 3.2 has the exact curl commands.
- Receipt export: receipts are available via the control-plane API and as a daily S3 bundle (we keep 90 days by default). We will include a signed index file for each bundle.
- Bastion pickup: default pickup window is every 60 minutes; can be configured down to 15 minutes at additional cost (more egress checks).

Action items:
1) Priya/Kimberly — attach the filled evidence bundle (SOC2 excerpt + sample receipts) to HUBSPOT-REC-99821.
2) Simon — please share the redaction-list by Mon EOD so we can run a scrub test.
3) Ops — we'll prepare a pre-provision checklist for firewall rules and cert publishing.

I've attached the runbook excerpt and network diagram for quick reference. If FinTrust would prefer an on-site install support window we can quote that as well.

Thanks all — Marissa
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

[Attachments: redwood-onprem-runbook-v1.4.md, network-egress-diagram.png]
